title: Counting atoms in formulae
keyIdea: A small number after a symbol counts that atom. A big number in front counts whole molecules. Brackets multiply everything inside.

kid: In H₂O, the small 2 belongs to the H. So there are 2 hydrogen atoms and 1 oxygen atom: 3 atoms in all.
A big number in front counts molecules. 3H₂O means 3 water molecules. That is 3 × 2 = 6 hydrogen atoms and 3 oxygen atoms.
adult: Brackets multiply everything inside them. In Ca(OH)₂ there is 1 calcium, 2 oxygen and 2 hydrogen atoms: 5 atoms in total.
Use both rules together when needed. 2Ca(OH)₂ has 2 calcium, 4 oxygen and 4 hydrogen atoms. In an equation, count each element on each side. A balanced equation has the same totals on both sides.

familyTip: Write formulae on cards (H₂O, CO₂, 2NH₃) and race each other to count the atoms.

practice.prompt: How many atoms in total are in one H₂O molecule?
How many hydrogen atoms are in {n}H₂O?
How many oxygen atoms are in Ca(OH)₂?
How many oxygen atoms are in {n}CO₂?

practice.hint: A big number in front counts molecules.

pool.prompt: How many atoms in total are in {n}CH₄?
How many oxygen atoms are in {n}Ca(OH)₂?
How many hydrogen atoms are in 2NH₃?
How many atoms in total are in Mg(NO₃)₂?
pool.hint: The bracket doubles N and O₃.

pool.prompt: How many oxygen atoms are in Al₂(SO₄)₃?
pool.explain: 4 oxygen atoms × 3 = 12. Adding 4 + 3 = 7 is a common slip.

pool.prompt: How many atoms of each element are in H₂SO₄?
pool.hint: Each small number belongs to the symbol just before it.
pool.explain: H₂ gives 2 H, S has no number so 1, O₄ gives 4.

pool.prompt: The right-hand side of an equation has {n}H₂O. How many hydrogen atoms must the left-hand side have?
pool.hint: Atoms are not made or destroyed.
pool.explain: {n} × 2 = {=2*n}, so the left needs {=2*n} hydrogen atoms too.
